wishbone_security_features.name: [LOCK_O] / [LOCK_I] locked bus cycle
wishbone_security_features.purpose: Indicates the current bus cycle is uninterruptible. Useful for indivisible semaphore operations (RMW + LOCK) and for preventing interleaved access from other MASTERs during a critical section.

wishbone_security_features.name: [TGA_O()] address tag with 'protected memory' encoding (user-defined)
wishbone_security_features.purpose: RULE 2.15 example — TGA tag may be used by memory-management hardware to indicate a protected address space. The tag's semantics are user-defined (DATASHEET-declared) but the spec acknowledges this as a recommended use case.

wishbone_security_features.name: [TGC_O()] cycle tag with 'interrupt acknowledge' or 'cache control' encoding (user-defined)
wishbone_security_features.purpose: Allows the MASTER to mark a bus cycle as a special class (interrupt-ack, cache-flush, etc.). Useful for restricted access policies. User-defined per DATASHEET.

wishbone_security_features.name: [ERR_O] / [ERR_I] abnormal termination
wishbone_security_features.purpose: Allows a SLAVE to reject an access (e.g. access to a protected region). The MASTER's reaction is IP-supplier-defined; integrators may map ERR_O to an access-control violation indicator.

what_is_NOT_in_the_spec: No confidentiality / encryption at the bus layer (no AES, no cipher).
No data-integrity / authentication (no MAC, no HMAC).

No formal secure/non-secure transfer signal (unlike AMBA AHB5 HNONSEC or AXI AxPROT[1]). Secure/non-secure partitioning, if required, must be implemented via user-defined TGA / TGC tags or by mapping protected regions to separate Wishbone segments behind access-control filters at the INTERCON level.
No formal privileged/user transfer signal (unlike AMBA HPROT[1] / PPROT[0]). Privileged-mode indication, if required, must be user-defined via TGA / TGC tags.
secure_integration_responsibilities: Address-space partitioning: integrator places SLAVEs at non-overlapping address regions and routes them through user-defined TGA tags or INTERCON-level access-control filters.
Atomic semaphore operations: use RMW + LOCK_O to ensure another MASTER cannot interleave a read-modify-write sequence (Section 3.4 + Section 2.2.3 LOCK_O).
Watchdog timeouts: INTERCON SHOULD include a watchdog (RECOMMENDATION 3.10) to detect a MASTER stuck asserting [STB_O] — also a denial-of-service prevention.
Optional ERR_O / RTY_O termination by SLAVE-side access-control filter: rejects accesses that violate the integrator's policy.
TrustZone-like or RoT-like primitives are out-of-scope and must be implemented by a dedicated upstream IP (TZASC, MMU/SMMU, Secure ROM).
fields.notes: Wishbone B4 security is limited to signaling primitives (LOCK + RMW + user-defined TGA/TGC tags + ERR_O / RTY_O termination) — not cryptographic primitives. End-to-end confidentiality and integrity must be provided by upper layers (dedicated crypto IP, secure boot ROM, address-space controllers). Wishbone's clear-text bus signaling is appropriate for on-chip use; off-chip extensions over public boards may require integrator-added bus-encryption wrappers.

evidence.quote: The lock output [LOCK_O] when asserted, indicates that the current bus cycle is uninterruptible. Lock is asserted to request complete ownership of the bus. Once the transfer has started, the INTERCON does not grant the bus to any other MASTER, until the current MASTER negates [LOCK_O] or [CYC_O].

Address tag type [TGA_O()] contains information associated with address lines [ADR_O()] ... For example, address size (24-bit, 32-bit etc.) and memory management (protected vs. unprotected) information can be attached to an address.

Cycle tag type [TGC_O()] contains information associated with bus cycles ... For example, data transfer, interrupt acknowledge and cache control cycles can be uniquely identified with the cycle tag. They can also be used to discriminate between WISHBONE SINGLE, BLOCK and RMW cycles.
The RMW (read-modify-write) cycle is used for indivisible semaphore operations.

Design INTERCON modules to prevent deadlock conditions. One solution is to include a watchdog timer function that monitors the MASTER's [STB_O] signal, and asserts [ERR_I] or [RTY_I] if the cycle exceeds some pre-defined time limit.
